# implement.py Key Files gate misses the bold-inside-heading form

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-31). That RISE item was filed during `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` and is deleted once this item exists (producer decision Q1 = re-file here).

**Headline:** The Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate in `implement.py` parses only
`## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)` and a bare `**Key Files:**` line, so a
work item whose section is written `## **Key Files:**` (bold marker nested in an
H2/H3) yields no key files, dirty-file relevance becomes unjudgeable, and
`implement.py start` aborts on a dirty checkout even when every dirty path is
unrelated. Make the heading matcher form-agnostic and lock it down with
regression tests.

## Problem statement

`_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` matches
`#{1,6}\s*Key Files.*` (heading) **or** `\*\*Key Files:?\*\*.*` (bold line) — but
not the combination `## **Key Files:**`, because after the `## ` prefix the next
token is `**`, not `Key Files`. `extract_key_files_from_description()` then
returns `[]`, `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` reports *"no Key Files section in
the work item description — cannot judge dirty-file relevance"*, and
`phase_start` takes the conservative abort-and-ask branch even though the
description does list key files and the dirty paths demonstrably do not overlap
them. The gate's conservative default is correct; it is being tripped by a
parser gap rather than by a real risk.

## Evidence

Reproduced in this session against the installed skill tree
(`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `SorraAgents/skill`):

| form | `extract_key_files_from_description` |
|---|---|
| `## Key Files` | `['a/b.ts', 'tests/c.test.ts']` |
| `## Key Files (predicted)` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `**Key Files:**` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `## **Key Files:**` | `[]` |
| `### **Key Files:**` | `[]` |

- **Corpus prevalence (consumer store):** 9 of 386 items in the
  `tce-the-rising` store use the bold-inside-heading form — the face-off tie
  epic parent RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU and its eight children
  (RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX, RISE-0MVRMI7GR006QH44, RISE-0MVRMI9F0007HXBW,
  RISE-0MVRMIB7Z008P1HB, RISE-0MVRMID1B0098HAY, RISE-0MVRMIF0T008A72W,
  RISE-0MVRMIGXS0073HDX, RISE-0MVRMIISC009TXYX). For comparison: 297 items use
  a plain heading, 52 a bare bold line, 28 none.
- **Observed stall:** `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` aborted on child
  RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX (Key Files: `tests/the-rising/risingMatchHarness.ts`,
  `tests/the-rising/TheRisingRules.test.ts`) although the only dirty paths were
  six untracked `standups/*.md` files — zero overlap, i.e. exactly the
  documented "proceed, leave the dirty files untouched" case. The operator
  worked around it by pre-creating the worktree and running `start` from inside
  it (where the main-checkout gate is skipped by design).
- **No direct test coverage** of `extract_key_files_from_description`,
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files` or `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` exists under
  `skill/implement/tests/`, so this class of gap is invisible to the suite.
- The framework does **not** emit the H2-wrapped form itself:
  `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` (`_parse_key_files_section`,
  `validate_key_files_format`) and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` use a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line, so both families of form must keep working.

## Users

- **Implement-skill agent (primary)**: "When I start an item whose Key Files
  section is written `## **Key Files:**`, I want `start` to read those paths and
  let me proceed when the dirty files are unrelated, so I do not have to
  hand-work around a gate that already has the information it needs."
- **Producer / operator (secondary)**: "When a downtime run dispatches a child
  session, I want `start` to proceed or abort for a real reason, so unattended
  runs do not stall on a parsing bug."
- **Framework maintainer**: "I want every accepted Key Files heading form
  covered by a table-driven test, so a future edit to the extractor cannot
  silently drop a form."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `extract_key_files_from_description()` returns the listed paths for
  any `Key Files` heading regardless of emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or
  case: `## **Key Files:**`, `### **Key Files:**`, `## **Key Files (predicted):**`,
  `#### key files`, asserted by a table-driven unit test in
  `skill/implement/tests/`.
- **AC2** — Every currently supported form keeps working, asserted in the same
  table: `## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)`, `### Key Files`, and a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line; plus the tolerant bare-marker variants —
  `  **Key Files:**` (indented/whitespace) and `**Key Files**` (no colon).
- **AC3** — `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` proceeds (`can_proceed: true`)
  when the description uses `## **Key Files:**` and the dirty paths do not
  overlap those entries, and still aborts (`can_proceed: false`) when a dirty
  path does overlap, or when the description has no Key Files section at all.
- **AC4** — Extraction still stops at the end of the Key Files section: a
  following `#`/`##`/`###` heading or standalone bold section marker terminates
  the list, so prose lines and acceptance-criteria bullets never leak in as
  paths (regression guard for the SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2 defect class).
- **AC5** — A regression test demonstrates the defect before the fix (red on the
  current implementation, green after), and the end-to-end path is verified:
  `implement.py start` on a `## **Key Files:**` item with only unrelated dirty
  paths creates the worktree, leaves the dirty files untouched and records the
  decision in a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — The gate's safety properties are preserved: no
  stash/commit/revert of dirty files, and abort-and-ask still fires for "no Key
  Files section" and for any overlap.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments and docstrings in `implement.py` and the accepted-forms
  list in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree
  gate, SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR) plus the project README and any relevant wiki or
  docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope is `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`** plus its tests and docs
  (producer decision Q2 = A). The two sibling parsers — `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  and `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — are fixed by linked follow-up
  items (below), not here.
- **The gate stays conservative.** No Key Files section, or any overlapping
  dirty path, must still abort and ask. Nothing here may turn the gate into a
  whitelist or relax "never stash/commit/revert the user's work".
- **Must not regress existing forms.** The new matcher may be more tolerant but
  never stricter: an item that starts cleanly today must still start cleanly.
- **Minimal surface.** No new configuration knob or environment variable.
- **UK English** in comments, docstrings and docs.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` (~line 1671),
  `extract_key_files_from_description()` (~1676),
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files()` (~1712), `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()`
  (~1742), and the `phase_start` call site (~5993) that turns a
  `can_proceed: false` verdict into the dirty-worktree abort.
- The extractor's loop already terminates on a `#`-heading line or a non-bullet
  line starting with `**`; only the initial heading match is wrong. A new
  matcher must not let the matched heading's own bold marker look like the
  section end.
- `skill/implement/tests/` has suites for the start/finish gates but none that
  exercises the Key Files extractor or the relevance classifier.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate
  section) enumerates the three supported forms and needs the tolerant list.

## Desired change

1. Replace the two-branch heading regex with one form-agnostic matcher: an
   optional H1–H6 prefix, an optional `**` bold marker, `Key Files`, an optional
   parenthetical qualifier and optional closing `**`/`:`, matched
   case-insensitively — while still requiring `Key Files` to be the first
   content token (so `## Notes on Key Files` stays unmatched unless it matches
   today).
2. Keep the section terminator and the bullet/backtick path parsing unchanged
   (including `path → note`).
3. Add the table-driven tests (AC1–AC5) and the end-to-end `start` regression.
4. Update the docstring/comment and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — form-agnostic `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE`,
  extractor terminator/docstrings; classifier branches unchanged.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_key_files_extraction.py` — new table-driven tests
  for the accepted forms, the terminator behaviour and
  `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` proceed/abort decisions.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — accepted-forms list in the
  Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate section.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — over/under-matching:** tightening "first content token" could make a
  heading that matches today (e.g. `## Key Files and notes`) stop matching.
  Keep the match at least as wide as today; assert the old forms in the table.
- **Risk — terminator drift:** after accepting the new form the loop must not
  treat the matched heading's own `**` as a section end.
- **Risk — untestable "it works now" claims:** the AC5 end-to-end check needs a
  deliberately dirty main checkout, so it must leave the dirty files untouched
  and clean up after itself (or exercise the classifier/`phase_start` seam
  directly).
- **Assumption:** the H2-wrapped form is agent-authored markdown, not framework
  output — so the fix belongs in the tolerant parser, not in the plan skill's
  emitter.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the plan/audit parsers are separate items (below);
  anything further discovered goes to `discovered-from` items, not this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR** — Allow implement.py start to create a clean worktree
  when main checkout is dirty: introduced the gate and the three-form parser;
  this item fixes its blind spot.
- **SA-0MUYEV5AO006V0HK** — project-local skill extensions / dirty-tree
  exemptions (the other documented relaxation path of the same gate).
- **SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2** — `plan_helpers._parse_key_files_section` did not stop
  at Markdown headings (same failure family: section-boundary parsing).
- **SA-0MTYP6T2I00396J7** — generated `standups/` output not gitignored: the
  source of the six dirty files in the reproduction.
- **SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ** — the previous framework fix discovered from a
  tce-the-rising implement run (disposition precedent for this re-filing).
- **RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU** — Face-off tie epic whose children carry the
  `## **Key Files:**` form and whose drive run hit the abort.

## Linked follow-up items (producer decision Q2 = B and C)

- **Follow-up 1 — plan parser:** `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  `_parse_key_files_section` / `validate_key_files_format` should accept the same
  heading forms so plan validation does not report a missing/empty Key Files
  section for a validly-written description.
- **Follow-up 2 — audit parser:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`'s Key
  Files extraction (`^#{0,4}\s*Key Files.*?$`) has the same blind spot, which
  omits the item's files from the Phase 2 file-scope manifest. Either fix it
  locally or extract one shared, heading-aware Key Files helper consumed by
  implement/plan/audit.

Both are filed with `discovered-from:<this item>`; their SA ids are recorded in
this item's comments.

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

Interview raised on RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (comment `RISE-C0MVWO1N400000N41`),
answered by the producer in-session on 2026-10-31. Answers are transcribed
verbatim.

- **Q1 — Which worklog/store carries the fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A - delete this when filed"** → the fix is re-filed in
  the SorraAgents worklog as this item (with `discovered-from:RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8`)
  and the RISE item is deleted once this item exists. Recommended option A was
  accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q2 — How wide is the parser fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A, with B and C as linked follow-ups"** →
  `implement.py` only in this item; the plan parser (B) and audit parser (C) are
  filed as linked follow-up items rather than folded in. Recommended option A
  was accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q3 — Which heading variants must be accepted?**
  **Answer (producer): "B + C"** → accept any `Key Files` heading regardless of
  emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or case (B), **and** tolerate whitespace /
  colon variants of the bare bold marker (C). Recommended option was B; the
  producer widened it to B+C, reflected in AC1/AC2. Source: interactive reply,
  this session.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — Does the framework emit the
  H2-wrapped form?** No: `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py:127-160` and
  `skill/plan/SKILL.md:181,306` specify a bare `**Key Files:**` line; the
  H2-wrapped form in the consumer store was authored into descriptions directly.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — How many items are affected in the
  consumer store?** 9 of 386 (`tce-the-rising`), all inside the face-off tie
  epic. Evidence: SQL scan of that store's `workitems.description`.

# plan Key Files parser misses the bold-inside-heading form

**discovered-from:SA-0MVWO79DA006FYCQ** (producer decision Q2 = B: fixed as a
linked follow-up, not folded into that item).

## Problem

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` parses the Key Files section with
`stripped.startswith("**Key Files:**")` (`_parse_key_files_section`, ~line 147)
and the same literal test in `validate_key_files_format` (~line 243). A
description that writes the section as a markdown heading with a nested bold
marker — `## **Key Files:**` — never matches, so the plan skill's completeness
validation treats the section as absent and `validate_key_files_format` either
reports success on an empty list or warns "section is present but contains no
valid file paths" depending on the code path.

# Test: push transport-retry policy

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC4, AC5). Test-first slice of the
transport-retry work.

## Why this must come first

Three pushes needed a manual retry loop after a green cached gate followed by
`Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` — `git_push_to_dev()`
currently returns `False` on any non-timeout, non-non-fast-forward failure, so
the caller cannot tell "retry later" from "fix the code". The retry policy
(retryable patterns, attempt bound, backoff, same cwd, no gate bypass) must be
pinned before it is implemented so the allowlist can never silently widen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test pins the retryable patterns: `Connection to … closed by remote host`, `Connection reset by peer`, `remote end hung up unexpectedly` and `kex_exchange_identification` are retried; auth, branch-policy and other errors are not.
- [ ] A test pins the attempt bound (initial attempt plus two retries) and jittered exponential backoff, and asserts a `PushTimeoutError` is never retried.
- [ ] A test asserts every attempt uses the **same cwd** as the first attempt and the same argv/env — no `--no-verify`, no `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP` or other bypass injection — so the pre-push gate runs again and serves its cached full-suite entry.
- [ ] A test asserts non-fast-forward failures keep their existing dedicated recovery (no transport retry) and that an exhausted retry trail reports the attempt count, the backoff used and the final reason.
- [ ] Stubs only (a fake `Popen`/process factory plus the hermetic git sandbox); no ad-hoc suite invocations and no real network access.
- [ ] Across the three test slices, new/updated tests cover FIFO fairness (cross-process), hook classification of slot-busy vs red suite vs timeout, finish reporting of a gate infrastructure failure, and transport-retry policy (retryable vs non-retryable stderr, attempt bound, same cwd) — tests use stubs/hermetic git sandboxes only, with no ad-hoc suite invocations.

## Minimal implementation

1. New module `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` with a
   recording fake process factory driven by a scripted stderr/return-code
   sequence, and a `time.sleep` spy for the backoff.
2. Table-driven cases for retryable vs non-retryable stderr.
3. Same-cwd / same-argv / same-env assertions across attempts.
4. Leave the tests red for the implementing slice.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — new: retry policy, attempt bound, same-cwd, no-bypass assertions
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` under test
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — existing push-timeout contract to stay consistent with

## Constraints

- Tests only; no production code in this slice.
- No network access and no real long sleeps (monkeypatch the sleep).
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- Retry-policy test module, red then green with the implementing slice.

## Dependencies

- None. Blocks the transport-retry implementation slice.

# Arrival-ordered turnstile in the shared semaphore

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC1, AC7). Implements the fairness half of the
starvation fix; the ordering tests come from the preceding test slice.

## Design (agreed direction — Q1 default (a), FIFO turnstile)

- A waiter takes a **monotonic ticket** in its namespace (a ticket file whose
  sequence comes from a flock-guarded counter), and **only the waiter holding
  the lowest outstanding ticket may attempt the slot scan**. Tickets are
  released on acquire, timeout, exception and crash.
- Ownership of a ticket is expressed as an exclusive `flock` on the ticket file
  itself, so the kernel releases it when the owner dies — a killed waiter's turn
  is reclaimed without PID bookkeeping and without stale state (crash-safety
  unchanged).
- The **fast path stays single-pass**: no outstanding lower ticket plus a free
  slot is one non-blocking scan, no ticket file written.
- Fairness is about *ordering*, not capacity: `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` is
  untouched. Staggered-wait jitter (SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD) is kept — it
  complements ordering (distinct deadlines), it is not replaced by it.
- Fail-fast callers (`timeout=0`, e.g. `audit_runner`) are **not** queued: an
  immediate attempt is unordered by definition (it is not a waiter), so it must
  still succeed instantly when a slot is free.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Semaphore.acquire()` in `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` grants a free slot to the oldest waiting arrival in its namespace (FIFO turnstile) instead of whichever waiter happens to poll next, so a waiter at queue position N is bounded by N × the expected hold time; the bound and the ordering contract are documented in the module docstring.
- [ ] Tickets are released on acquire, timeout, exception and crash (flock-backed, so a killed waiter's turn is reclaimed); no stale ticket can hold the queue.
- [ ] `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` is unchanged (ordering only, never capacity) and the staggered-wait jitter contract still holds.
- [ ] Fail-fast (`timeout=0`) callers still acquire immediately when a slot is free, and nested `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` namespaces stay isolated from the host-wide turnstile.
- [ ] The fairness, crash-reclaim, fail-fast and nested-isolation tests from the preceding test slice pass.
- [ ] The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add the ticket layer to `Semaphore` (`_take_ticket`, `_ticket_is_head`,
   `_release_ticket`) with the turnstile consulted inside `acquire()`'s loop.
2. Reclaim abandoned tickets by attempting a non-blocking flock on the lowest
   ticket file and unlinking it when the owner is gone.
3. Update the module docstring: ordering contract, wait bound (N × expected
   hold time), crash-reclaim mechanism, fail-fast exemption, nested isolation.
4. Keep the audit-semaphore (`jitter=0.0`) and test-skill (`jitter=0.1`)
   call sites unchanged — no config or env churn.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — ticket/turnstile layer, docstring contract and wait bound
- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — unit-level fairness and fast-path tests (produced by the preceding test slice)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrency_guard.py` — cross-process ordering and crash-reclaim tests (produced by the preceding test slice)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — slot-lane wrapper, unchanged (it is the main consumer)

## Constraints

- Do **not** change `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` / `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST` or any ceiling.
- Keep the kernel-`flock` crash-safety property; no PID files, no daemons, no lock timeouts that can leave stale state.
- The turnstile must not add more than a couple of flock operations per attempt (a latency regression here multiplies across every suite run).
- Repository boundaries: framework source only; consumers receive it via `scripts/install_pi.sh`.
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- Fair, starvation-bounded `Semaphore` with documented bound, plus green fairness tests.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the FIFO fairness test slice (which blocks this item).

# Gate-reason classifier and pre-push diagnostics

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC3). Implements the hook half of the
dev-push reporting work.

## Design (agreed direction — Q4 default: reuse the runner's codes)

- One shared classifier (new module) is the single source of truth for the
  mapping runner-result → `gate_reason`. It **consumes** the runner's published
  codes (`NOTICE_SLOT_BUSY`, `NOTICE_SUITE_TIMEOUT`, `NOTICE_KILLED`,
  `NOTICE_UNPARSED_FAILURE`, `NOTICE_COMMAND_NOT_FOUND`) plus the structural
  facts (`failures`, `live_repo_mutation`, unparsable output) — it never
  re-defines or forks them (they are owned by SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z).
- Published `gate_reason` values: `slot_busy`, `suite_timeout`, `killed`,
  `unparsed_failure`, `command_not_found`, `test_failure`, `infrastructure`.
- `.githooks/pre-push` captures the runner's `--json` stdout into a temporary
  file (instead of discarding it), prints a stable `gate_reason=<code>` line on
  stderr plus a distinct human message, and still exits non-zero in every
  failure case.
- Resolution: repo-local `skill/shared/gate_reason.py`, else
  `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/shared/gate_reason.py` (the same pattern the release
  script uses), else `gate_reason=infrastructure` — never fail-open.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.githooks/pre-push` consumes the runner's machine-readable result (no longer a discarded `--json` blob) and prints distinct diagnostics — a stable `gate_reason=<code>` line plus a human message — for slot contention, timeout, killed and unparsed runs versus genuine test failures.
- [ ] The hook still exits non-zero in every failure case (never fail-open), and its message for a red suite is unchanged in substance.
- [ ] The classifier maps each published runner notice code and the structural facts to one published `gate_reason` value; structured failures always win, so a genuine code failure is never reported as infrastructure.
- [ ] The classifier is resolvable from a consumer repo (repo-local, then installed global skill, then a conservative `infrastructure` fallback) and is unit-testable without executing the hook.
- [ ] The hook classification tests from the preceding test slice pass.

## Minimal implementation

1. New module `skill/shared/gate_reason.py`: `classify(result: dict) -> str`
   plus a CLI that reads the runner's JSON on stdin and prints the code.
2. Rewrite the hook's gate block: `json_out="$(mktemp)"`, run the runner with
   `--json >"$json_out" 2>"$err_out"`, classify on failure, print
   `gate_reason=<code>` and the per-reason message, `exit 1`.
3. Keep the existing red-suite wording (and the `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` hint).
4. Bump the hook's `worklog:pre-push-hook:v3` marker so installed hooks are
   refreshed by `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/shared/gate_reason.py` — new: canonical runner-result → `gate_reason` classifier (plus CLI), reused by the `.githooks/pre-push` hook script
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — the notice-code constants the classifier consumes (consumption only, no re-definition)
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — hook wiring and version marker for the updated `.githooks/pre-push` hook script (JSON capture, `gate_reason=` line and per-reason diagnostics)

## Constraints

- Consume, do not re-define, the runner's notice codes or the finish-gate `GATE_FAILURE_*` vocabulary (SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z owns those).
- Never fail-open: an unparsable or missing JSON result must still block the push.
- POSIX `sh` only (no bashisms beyond what the hook already uses); the hook must stay fast when the suite is green.
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- Shared classifier and a hook that reports *why* the dev-push gate failed.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the gate_reason classification test slice. Blocks the finish-reporting slice.

# Bounded transport-close retry in git_push_to_dev

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC4, AC7). Implements the retry half of the
flake fix; the retry-policy tests come from the preceding test slice.

## Design (agreed direction — Q3 default)

- 3 attempts total (initial + 2 retries), jittered exponential backoff
  (~2 s, ~8 s, capped), retrying **only** the allowlisted transport patterns:
  `Connection to … closed by remote host`, `Connection reset by peer`,
  `remote end hung up unexpectedly`, `kex_exchange_identification`.
- Auth, branch-policy and every other error keeps today's behaviour;
  non-fast-forward keeps its existing dedicated rebase-and-retry recovery;
  `PushTimeoutError` is never retried (a timeout means the gate was running —
  replaying it multiplies cost).
- Every attempt uses the same cwd, argv and environment: the retry runs the
  pre-push hook again, which serves its cached full-suite entry. No bypass
  flag is ever injected.
- The attempt trail (count, backoff used, final reason) is logged and returned
  to the caller for reporting.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Transient transport closes are retried with bounded backoff: `git_push_to_dev()` retries a transport-level close (`Connection to … closed by remote host`, `Connection reset by peer`, `remote end hung up unexpectedly`, `kex_exchange_identification`) up to a bounded number of attempts with jittered exponential backoff, from the **same cwd** as the first attempt.
- [ ] It fails fast (no retry) on auth, branch-policy and non-fast-forward errors, and never retries a push timeout.
- [ ] The retry does not bypass the gate: the pre-push hook runs again and serves its cached full-suite entry, and the attempt count, backoff and reason are logged and reported.
- [ ] The push cwd stays whatever the caller resolved — the retry reuses it and hard-codes nothing, so the push-from-worktree change can land without rework.
- [ ] The transport-retry tests from the preceding test slice pass, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add a transport-close allowlist predicate and retry constants (attempts,
   backoff base, cap) with injectable overrides for tests.
2. Wrap the existing spawn/communicate logic in a bounded attempt loop,
   preserving process-group kill on timeout and the non-fast-forward detection.
3. Log each attempt (`attempt i/N`, reason, backoff) and carry the trail on the
   raised/reported failure.
4. No change to call sites' signatures (`-> bool` stays; richer failures are
   raised).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` transport allowlist, attempt loop and backoff
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — retry-policy tests (produced by the preceding test slice)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_abort.py` — finish interplay to keep green
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — non-fast-forward recovery must stay non-retried

## Constraints

- Only the recognised transport patterns retry — everything else fails as today (a retry must never mask a real error).
- Do not hard-code `repo_root` as the push cwd: reuse the caller's cwd (coordinate with SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN / SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3, which change it).
- Do not assume the keepalive fix (SA-0MVWNHLQQ002TFZR) has landed; the retry is the general safety net.
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- A dev push that survives a transient transport close without a manual retry loop, with a visible attempt trail.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the transport-retry test slice.

Discovered-from: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (during `/skill:plan`).

## Problem

`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` runs the full-suite release
gate as:

```bash
if python3 "$TEST_RUNNER" --scope full --strict-git-env 2>&1; then
```

The runner's machine-readable result is never requested and the exit code is
the only signal, so a slot-contention expiry (`slot_busy`), a killed suite
(`killed`) and a genuine red suite all produce the same message: "Full test
suite failed on the merged dev→main tree — the release is blocked." The
operator cannot tell "fix the code" from "wait for a slot / raise
`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`", and a release attempt can burn hours of queue wait before
failing indistinguishably from a real regression.

The pre-push hook gets the equivalent fix under **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (its
AC2/AC3); this item is the same defect on the release path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The release gate consumes the runner's machine-readable result and reports the same `gate_reason=<code>` vocabulary the pre-push hook uses.
- [ ] A slot-contention or killed-run failure prints a distinct message with the remediation hint (wait then re-run, or raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`), while a red suite keeps its current message.
- [ ] The gate still fails closed (non-zero exit, no release) in every failure case, and `SHIP_TEST_SKIP=1` still bypasses it.
- [ ] A hermetic test (following `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py`) pins the classification for slot contention, killed and red-suite cases.

## Notes

- Reuse the shared classifier introduced by SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI rather than a second copy; this item is deliberately **not** a child of it so the release path can ship independently.
- UK English throughout.
data.title: Release gate (merge-dev-to-main.sh) discards the runner JSON, so a dev→main release cannot say why the suite gate failed

# Live-repo guard fails a run when a concurrent `wl sync` moves `refs/heads/worklog/data`

## Target outcome

A full-suite run must not be failed — and must not lose its green cache entry —
because another agent's concurrent `wl sync` moved the Worklog data ref.

**Observed** while finishing SA-0MVQQ9KZO0010XXS (2026-11-01):

```
run_tests.py --scope full → success: false
live-repo mutation detected: … moved ref refs/heads/worklog/data:
  0067d646089788ee530ff8856bd481d7bd1cd7c7 -> 96ea6f021c940ed2374e353de9f1df84f9438e6d
  (in the worktree AND in the main checkout)
```

Every test suite passed (`suites.all.returncode == 0`, 835/835 node tests, pytest
green), but the outer guard's verdict forces `success: false`, so no green
full-suite cache entry is written, and `implement.py finish`'s gate reports
"infrastructure reason" with no structured failures.

## Root cause

`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` excludes `refs/worklog/*` (`WORKLOG_REF_PREFIX`)
from the mutation surface, but the Worklog data ref also lives — and moves —
under `refs/heads/worklog/data`. Concurrent `wl sync` (sibling `implement.py
finish` pushes, the herdr downtime worker) moves it while any suite runs, so the
guard reports it as a mutation of the guarded checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Excluded as concurrency churn.** `refs/heads/worklog/data`
  (and the `refs/heads/worklog/` namespace generally) is excluded from the
  live-repo mutation surface, derived from the ref name (never a work-item
  pattern), reported instead as an informational note.
- [ ] **AC2 — Regression pinned.** A test snapshots a fixture checkout, moves
  `refs/heads/worklog/data` externally, and asserts `_detect_live_repo_mutation`
  reports no mutation (note only).
- [ ] **AC3 — Suite-caused data movement still fails.** A suite that itself
  commits to `refs/heads/worklog/data` remains a mutation (the exclusion is
  provenance independent only if the guard cannot distinguish; if it cannot,
  document the blind spot explicitly in `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`).

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (`WORKLOG_REF_PREFIX`, mutation surface)
- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` / `tests/test_guarded_roots.py`
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`

## Related work

- `discovered-from:SA-0MVQQ9KZO0010XXS`
- WL-0MVPE2B8E005O0OS / SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX — guarded-roots provenance work.

## Impact

Blocks any item whose finish requires a full-scope gate while other agents are
active: the green run cannot be cached, so `implement.py finish` cannot reach
its terminal status write, and audits see a cache miss.
data.title: Live-repo guard treats a concurrent wl sync (refs/heads/worklog/data) as a suite mutation

data.description:
## Goal

As the operator, I want the 2026-10-31 test-slot starvation fix proved shut with post-fix
measurements, and the remaining cross-consumer duplicate-suite vector removed, so that no agent
session loses minutes queueing for a 1–3 s test run and no two consumers pay twice for the same
full suite.

## Problem statement

The fast-lane fix (`SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`, shipped `a2659c38` on 2026-10-31T23:21) delivered the
separate `test-fast` semaphore namespace, the re-derived `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT = 6` and
the `slot_wait_seconds`/`slot_lane` reporting. Two gaps remain from the original RCA item
(`LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM`, llm repo — closed as superseded by `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`):

1. **No post-fix measurement.** Its AC5 ("median blocked time per work item falls materially below
   ~10 min/test call; evidence recorded") was never executed. A preliminary scan of the 30 pi
   session logs touched since `a2659c38` found 12 `slot_wait_seconds` samples, all `0.00 s`, and
   zero `queued N s for a <lane>-lane slot` notices — encouraging, but too small a sample to close
   the question, and it says nothing about the two dominant wait categories (`implement finish` and
   the dev-push full-suite gate), which appear as `wait_for_job` blocks, not `run_tests.py` JSON.
2. **Verdicts are not reusable across consumers.** `run_cached()` keys on either the loose worktree
   fingerprint or — when the caller passes an explicit would-be-commit tree SHA — on
   `fingerprint_kind="tree"`. `implement.py` finish passes a tree SHA; the pre-push gate, the test
   CLI and the audit path pass nothing and therefore keep historical loose-worktree keys
   (`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § "Explicit-fingerprint override" says so outright). A green
   full-suite verdict therefore cannot be carried between the pre-commit staged tree and the pushed
   commit, so a dev push re-executes the full suite even when an identical tree was validated
   minutes earlier.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — needs evidence, not anecdotes, that the critical starvation fix worked:
  *As the operator, I want a recorded p50/p90/max of post-fix slot wait so I can close the RCA with
  data rather than with the fix's assertion.*
- **Agent session** — *As an agent pushing to `dev`, I want the gate to reuse a green verdict for
  the tree I am pushing so my push does not cost a second 7–9 minute suite run.*

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` + `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`: two lanes
  (`test`, `test-fast`), ceilings 6 and 4, `slot_wait_seconds`/`slot_lane`/`slot_lanes` reported,
  `queued N s for a <lane>-lane slot` notice at ≥ 1 s.
- `skill/test_cache.py`: `compute_tree_state(index_file)` → `git write-tree` SHA;
  `run_cached(..., fingerprint=<sha>)` keys lookup and store with
  `FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE`; `query_cached()` stays worktree-only by design.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: finish no longer runs a full suite at all — it defers to
  the dev-push gate (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`) and passes the tree SHA for its changed-scope verdict
  (`SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB`).
- `.githooks/pre-push` (SorraAgents, v3): full-suite gate runs
  `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` with **no** `--fingerprint`, i.e. worktree-keyed.
  It also **ignores the pushed `local_sha`** entirely (only `remote_ref` selects the gate), so the
  suite validates whatever the checkout happens to contain — there is no pushed-commit guard in
  this hook yet (the `llm` repo's diverged v4 hook has one: `LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9`).
  `.githooks/pre-push.v2` (installed into other projects) deliberately has no suite gate, so it
  needs no change. Per-repo hooks diverge: `~/projects/llm/.githooks/pre-push` is a separate v4
  variant with its own pushed-commit guard and a `--project-root` argument.

## Desired change

1. Re-measure the post-fix wait distribution and record it (with the method) in this item.
2. Give the pre-push full-suite gate a pushed-commit guard and a tree-keyed fingerprint (plumbed
   through the runner CLI), so the gate measures the tree it pushes and its verdict lands in the
   same namespace as the finish gate's, and is reused when the tree matches.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Post-fix re-measurement recorded.** A reproducible analysis (commands/script cited in the item)
   over every pi session log covering at least 24 h after `a2659c38` (or all sessions since
   2026-10-31T23:21 if fewer) reports, per wait category — (a) `run_tests.py` slot wait, (b)
   `implement finish`, (c) dev-push full-suite gate — the call count and p50/p90/max wall clock.
   Pass: no run reports `slot_wait_seconds > 120 s`, partial-run (`test-fast`) p90 < 30 s, and no
   `queued N s` notice ≥ 30 s. Any miss is recorded honestly and filed as follow-up work, not
   smoothed over.
2. **The pre-push gate keys on the pushed tree.** The gate first adds the pushed-commit guard this
   hook currently lacks (pushed `local_sha` must equal the checkout's `HEAD` and the tree must be
   clean, with a loud refusal naming the commit, the HEAD, the tree path and the recovery step —
   the `llm` v4 hook's wording is the precedent), then computes that commit's tree SHA and passes
   it explicitly, so the verdict is stored and looked up with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`. When the
   guard fails or the tree SHA cannot be computed the gate refuses rather than falling back to a
   loose worktree key (fail-closed, matching the cache's provenance contract).
3. **Cross-consumer reuse proven.** A test demonstrates that a full-suite verdict recorded for tree
   *T* by one caller (finish gate / tree-keyed `run_cached`) is served as a cache hit to the
   pre-push gate for the same *T*, and that a different tree misses. The gate reports cache
   hit/miss (and the reused entry's age) in its stderr/JSON output so a served verdict is visible.
4. **Runner CLI surface + docs.** `run_tests.py` accepts an explicit tree fingerprint for
   `--scope full` (the parameter already threads through `run_suite`/`run_all`), documented in
   `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`; `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` and the hook's header comment are
   updated — the "callers that pass nothing keep worktree keys … (test-skill CLI, audit, pre-push)"
   sentence must no longer describe the pre-push gate.
5. **Tests.** Deterministic tests cover: the gate computes and passes the pushed tree SHA; a
   same-tree second run is a hit; a different tree is a miss; fail-closed when `HEAD != local_sha`,
   when the tree is dirty, or when the tree SHA is unavailable; worktree-keyed callers' cache keys
   are unchanged byte for byte. Existing cache/provenance, finish-gate-tree and pre-push hook tests
   stay green.
6. **Rollout is explicit, not implicit.** The item records that the `llm` repo's diverged v4 hook
   needs its own change (follow-up item), and that `pre-push.v2` consumers are unaffected.
7. **Testing/validation criterion.** Every new behaviour above is exercised by an automated test
   that fails before the change and passes after it, executed through the test skill.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant docs-site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Repository scope:** implementation lands in this repo only (`skill/test_cache.py`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `.githooks/pre-push`, docs, tests). The `llm` repo's v4 hook is
  a follow-up in that repo; `ContextHub` and others receive `pre-push.v2` (no suite gate) and need
  nothing.
- **No synthetic saturation.** Measurement must be read-only log analysis; the host is live and a
  synthetic burst would manufacture the very contention being measured (same deliberate scope
  decision as `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`).
- **Cache correctness first.** Never degrade to a state-independent fallback key and never serve a
  tree verdict for a different tree; an unfingerprintable run simply executes fresh.
- **POSIX `sh` hook.** No new dependency, no `bash`-isms in `.githooks/pre-push`.
- **Test execution policy.** All test runs go through the test skill (`run_tests.py`); no ad-hoc
  `pytest` invocations.
- **Do not edit the pacer/lane semantics** delivered by `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` — this item only
  measures them and changes cache keying.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test_cache.py` — tree-SHA helper usable from a committed (not just staged) state, plus the
  existing `fingerprint_kind` plumbing.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — CLI flag for an explicit tree fingerprint, threaded to
  `run_suite`/`run_all`/`run_cached`.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — add the pushed-commit guard, compute `HEAD^{tree}`, pass it, report hit/miss.
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` — same-tree hit / different-tree miss / fail-closed cases.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py` — cross-consumer reuse assertion.
- `tests/unit/test-pre-push-hook.mjs` — hook-level assertions (flag presence, refusal paths).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — contract updates.
- Measurement: pi session logs under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` plus existing tooling in
  `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` as the pattern for a one-off analysis script.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — measurement window is thin.** ~13 h of post-fix logs with 12 samples today; if the
  window yields too few samples the criterion is "no regression observed in N samples", clearly
  labelled, with a re-check date. *Mitigation:* report sample counts alongside percentiles.
- **Risk — cache poisoning by a wrong tree key.** A bug here could serve a green verdict for an
  untested tree. *Mitigation:* fail closed, plus explicit same-tree/different-tree tests and reuse of
  the already-audited `fingerprint_kind` machinery.
- **Risk — hook divergence drift.** Per-repo copies (`llm` v4, `pre-push.v2`) mean the fix can land
  in `SorraAgents` yet not reach a project. *Mitigation:* AC6 + a follow-up item per diverged hook.
- **Risk — scope creep into the wider RCA amplifiers** (`drive` nested waits, finish lock
  serialisation, agents raising `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` to 5400 s). Recorded as linked follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption —** the dominant residual cost is the dev-push gate suite, not finish, because finish
  no longer runs a full suite (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`). The AC1 measurement either confirms or
  refutes this, and refutation re-opens the amplifier list rather than silently narrowing the item.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` — fast lane + calibrated ceiling + `slot_wait` reporting (**shipped
  `a2659c38`**); supersedes AC1–AC3 of the original RCA.
- `LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM` (llm) — the original RCA item; closed as superseded, its AC4 residual and
  AC5 re-measurement are this item's scope.
- `SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81` — full-suite testing deferred to the dev-push gate (makes AC4 of the old
  item largely obsolete and creates the reuse gap addressed here).
- `SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB` / `SA-0MVQHVKUH009VQMD` — tree-bound finish verdicts and their documented
  contract (the precedent this item extends to the pre-push gate).
- `SA-0MVU8XRBQ000DG9D` — runner duration/timeout/kill/slot-wait facts (source of
  `slot_wait_seconds`).
- Open amplifiers, already tracked: `SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0` (a low-ceiling waiter never probes
  higher-numbered free slots), `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI` (dev pushes starve/flake under load),
  `SA-0MVEEALZR0029DD7` (single-flight coalescing of identical in-flight suite runs).
- `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` — finish gate: classify timeouts/kills and report slot queue wait separately.
- Pushed-commit-guard precedents: `LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9` (llm v4 hook guard),
  `LP-0MVTI2K2A002HCGT` (llm: gate validated the main checkout, not the pushed commit — completed).
- Adjacent, open, *not* in scope: `SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3` / `SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3` (implement.py must
  push from the tree it is pushing) and `SA-0MVV1V1DB0035Q6B` (gate did not execute for the pushed
  commit) — they concern which tree `finish` pushes, not the hook's own fingerprint.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (producer, interactive reply):** "`SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` already holds AC1–AC3; what should
  happen to `LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM`?" — Options: (a) close as superseded and file the residual here,
  (b) narrow the `llm` item and implement cross-repo, (c) close as fully superseded and drop
  AC4/AC5.
  **Answer: "1. A"** — close the `llm` item as superseded; the residual (AC4 gap + AC5
  re-measurement) is filed as this item. Source: interactive reply, this session. Research:
  verified `a2659c38` in `SorraAgents` (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT == 6`, `test-fast` lane,
  live `slot_lane=fast`, `slot_wait=0.00007s`); verified none of the named files exist in the `llm`
  checkout, so an `llm`-store item could not satisfy worktree isolation.
- **Q2 (producer, interactive reply):** "Residual scope?" — Options: (a) re-measure only,
  (b) re-measure + tree-keyed pre-push gate, (c) re-measure + the wider amplifiers from the RCA.
  **Answer: "2. b"**; producer also asked for follow-up work to be recommended and offered as new
  work items rather than silently folded in. Source: interactive reply, this session. Research:
  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § "Explicit-fingerprint override" documents that the pre-push
  gate keys on loose worktree state; `run_cached`/`run_suite` already accept an explicit tree
  fingerprint, so the change is a CLI + hook plumbing problem, not a cache redesign.
- **Q3 (agent, resolved by inspection, no producer input needed):** "Does `implement finish` still run
  a full suite whose verdict the pre-push gate could reuse?" — **Answer: no**; finish defers the
  full suite to the dev-push gate (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`, `fe85415a`, 2026-10-19), which is why the
  old AC4 is re-scoped to cross-consumer keying rather than finish→pre-push handoff. Source:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` step 3b comment.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVWNHLQQ002TFZR** – GitHub closes the idle SSH connection during the pre-push full-suite gate, silently discarding a green gate (open)
- **SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG** – Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md after git pull (completed)
- **SA-0MQVIXRSE000AYCA** – Convert /plan command to a pi skill with bundled helpers (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+421 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+395 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, 0mvqhvhxi007pqab, ac1, ac3, ac4 (+380 more)

Discovered-from: **SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU** (during intake).

## Problem

The herdr downtime round-robin cursor at `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` still carries `/home/rgardler/projects/open_source_llm`, a project directory that no longer exists. The stale entry is never served (no instance offers it) but it pollutes the managed-root view and can lead an operator or a scheduled-prompt provisioning helper to treat a deleted project as live.

## Desired change

Remove the stale `open_source_llm` entry from the round-robin cursor (and any other root whose directory no longer exists) via a safe, idempotent cleanup — either a small maintenance command that prunes non-existent roots or an operator-documented manual edit. Do not remove roots whose directory exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The round-robin cursor no longer contains `/home/rgardler/projects/open_source_llm`, while every root whose directory exists is preserved.
2. The cleanup is idempotent (a second run makes no change) and reports what it pruned.
3. A test covers the prune (stale root removed, existing roots preserved, second run a no-op), or — if the cleanup is manual — the documented procedure is verified on the live file.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Summary

`implement.py start <id>` fails to resume an existing, registered worktree when it is invoked from **inside** that worktree — the documented driven-child resume path (a driven child session calls `start` for its own item from its cwd inside the pre-created worktree). It computes a cwd-relative default worktree path and then resolves it against the worktree, producing a doubly-nested path, so the resume check misses and `git worktree add` fails.

Discovery report: **AH-0MVWTCIV9008ZCEY** (`discovered-from:AH-0MVWTCIV9008ZCEY`), filed in the AI_Hell worklog. The fix is tracked here because `implement.py` lives in this repository (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) and cannot be implemented from the AI_Hell worktree.

## Reproduction (observed 2026-10-31 during AH-0MVSE7F090010EG3)

1. Worktree `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<ID>-<slug>` exists and is registered (`.git` is a file; `git worktree list` shows it).
2. `cd` into that worktree and run `python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py start <ID>`.
3. Output: `INFO: Refreshing parent branch dev...`, then `INFO: Creating worktree at .worklog/worktrees/wl-<ID>-<slug> from branch dev...`, then `ERROR: Failed to create worktree at ...`; the item is released to `open`.

## Root cause

In `phase_start` / `_phase_start_locked()`:

- `wt_path = worktree_path_override or worktree_path_for(work_item_id, slug)`
- `worktree_path_for()` returns a path **relative to the repo root** (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`)
- `abs_wt_path = str(Path(wt_path).resolve())` resolves that relative path against `cwd`

When `cwd` is the item's own worktree, `abs_wt_path` becomes `<worktree>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`; `_is_worktree(abs_wt_path)` is `False`, so `git_worktree_add()` is attempted at the nested path and fails (and would have created a stray nested tree inside the worktree).

## Expected behaviour

`start` run from inside the item's own worktree resumes it — identical to running it from the main checkout: no `git worktree add`, the reported/recorded path is the existing absolute worktree path, and no nested `.worklog/worktrees/...` directory appears inside the worktree.

## Desired change

1. Resolve the **default** worktree path against the main checkout root (`_get_repo_root()`), not `cwd`; keep the existing fallback to `Path.cwd()` when `_get_repo_root()` returns `None`.
2. Keep `--worktree-path` authoritative and its semantics unchanged: an absolute override is used as given, a relative override continues to resolve against `cwd` (document this explicitly).
3. Use the resolved absolute path consistently for the resume check, `git_worktree_add`, the start/resume comment, the state file, the signal globals and the `cd <path>` hint.
4. Add a regression test that builds a **real** temporary git repo plus a linked worktree, runs `phase_start` with `cwd` inside the worktree and **does not mock `_get_repo_root`** (same fixture discipline as `skill/implement/tests/test_repo_root_resolution.py`, which exists precisely because mocking `_get_repo_root` hid a sibling defect).
5. Update the docs that state the resolution rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** `implement.py start <id>` invoked with `cwd` inside the item's own registered worktree resumes that worktree — the report/comment says resumed, `git_worktree_add` is not called, and no nested `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` path is created inside the worktree.
- **AC2:** The default worktree path is resolved against the main checkout root from `_get_repo_root()` (never `cwd`); when `_get_repo_root()` returns `None` the previous `cwd` fallback is preserved.
- **AC3:** Running `start` from the main checkout still creates the worktree at `<main-checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` (no regression).
- **AC4:** `--worktree-path` remains authoritative with unchanged semantics (absolute used as given; relative resolved against `cwd`) and that semantics is documented.
- **AC5:** A regression test covers AC1 with a real temp git repo + linked worktree and no `_get_repo_root` mocking, and fails against the pre-fix implementation.
- **AC6:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — at minimum the `phase_start` docstring/comment, `worktree_path_for()` docstring, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (resume-from-worktree wording) and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (path-resolution rule).
- **AC7:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_phase_start_locked()` (worktree path computation, resume check, `git_worktree_add` argument), `worktree_path_for()` docstring, `_get_repo_root()` reuse.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_worktree_resume.py` — new regression tests (real git fixtures; optionally reuse helpers from `test_repo_root_resolution.py`).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — resume-from-worktree wording ("`start` resumes the pre-created worktree idempotently").
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — path-resolution rule (`repo_root` section).

## Assumptions

- `--worktree-path` semantics stay unchanged to avoid breaking callers that pass paths relative to their cwd; only the default path changes.
- A related gap is out of scope and tracked separately: when the work item title (and therefore `slug`) changes after the worktree was created, `start` recomputes a different canonical path and still fails to resume — see the linked slug-drift follow-up.

## Related work

- Discovery report: `AH-0MVWTCIV9008ZCEY` (AI_Hell worklog).

data.description:
## Summary

`implement.py start` derives the canonical worktree path **and** branch name from the work item's *current* title slug (`worktree_path_for()` / `branch_name_for()`). If the title is edited after the worktree was created, `start` computes a different path and branch, so:

- the resume check (`_is_worktree(abs_wt_path)`) misses the existing worktree, and
- `git worktree add -b <new-branch> .worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<new-slug> dev` **succeeds**, silently creating a second, empty worktree for the same item while the real in-progress work stays in the old one.

`phase_start` never consults `_discover_worktree()` (which does scan `.worklog/worktrees/`), unlike `finish`/`abort`/`parent`.

## Why it matters

A driven child (or any resumed session) can then implement into the wrong tree or lose track of prior work; `finish` may remove the emptier tree while the real work is stranded. Title edits are a normal operator action (clarifying scope during planning).

## Expected behaviour

`start` should resume the item's **existing** worktree (and its existing branch) even when the current title slug differs from the directory/branch name created at start time. A second worktree must never be created for an item that already has one.

## Suggested approach

- Before computing a fresh path, consult the existing-discovery mechanism (`_discover_worktree`, or a `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-*/` scan that checks `.implement_state.json` / registered worktree branches for the item id) and reuse the found path and its checked-out branch.
- Fall back to the current path/slug computation only when no worktree exists for the item.
- Add a regression test: real git repo + worktree created for slug A, then `wl` title changed to slug B, then `start` from the main checkout (and from inside the worktree) — assert one worktree only, no new branch, and the report names the existing path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** After the work item title changes, `start` resumes the existing worktree and branch for the item instead of creating a second worktree/branch.
- **AC2:** `start` run from inside the existing (old-slug) worktree resumes it after a title change.
- **AC3:** When no worktree exists for the item, behaviour is unchanged (fresh path/branch from the current title slug).
- **AC4:** Regression tests cover AC1–AC3 with a real temporary git repo plus linked worktree.
- **AC5:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC6:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Related work

- Discovered while scoping `SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF` (resume from inside a linked worktree); discovery report `AH-0MVWTCIV9008ZCEY`.
- Out of scope for that fix: it only corrects the *base* against which the default path is resolved.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_phase_start_locked()`, `_discover_worktree()`, `worktree_path_for()`, `branch_name_for()`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_worktree_resume.py` (or a new slug-drift test module) — real git fixtures.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — resume semantics wording.

# Goal

Choose the design that makes the implement run's terminal lifecycle write
(`completed` / `in_review` plus the assignee release) the **last** lifecycle
action of the run, and record the decision plus the resulting hold/transition
contract so the test, implementation and docs items can proceed without
re-litigating it.

Part of parent **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** (Only mark as complete when fully complete).

## Context

Parent AC1 forbids any observable `completed`/`in_review` + cleared-assignee
window while an implement-run step remains. Today `phase_finish` writes the
terminal transition inside its `StatusLifecycle` block and then returns, while
`skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9 still requires post-push verification,
worktree cleanup and the completion comment afterwards — that is the window in
which the herdr downtime dispatcher can dispatch an audit that races the
still-running session.

Parent candidate designs (the implement phase may choose):
(A) verify-then-transition — move the post-push work inside `phase_finish`
before the `StatusLifecycle` exit;
(B) two-phase finish — `finish` keeps the item `in_progress` with the assignee
held and a final `implement.py complete` performs the transition;
(C) session-active hold — keep the assignee hold until the session's final
step, with documented bounded stale-hold reclamation.

## Scope

Decision and contract documentation only. **No code or test changes.**

## Work

1. Read the current transition sites: `phase_finish` (terminal transition in
   the `StatusLifecycle` block, `_assert_terminal_status` read-back),
   `phase_parent` (parent advancement), `_finalise_stranded_child` (driven
   stranded child), `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`
   Step 9 and the status-transition matrix.
2. Evaluate A/B/C against parent AC1–AC5 and the parent constraints
   (preserve the assignee-hold convention and release-by-default; preserve
   `_assert_terminal_status`; preserve idempotence/recovery; no dispatcher
   change; no scope creep into ContextHub).
3. Decide and record, in a comment on this item **and** on the parent:
   - the chosen design and the rationale, naming which parent AC each rejected
     option fails;
   - the exact ordered finalisation steps inside `phase_finish` (up to and
     including the terminal write and the read-back assertion);
   - which steps remain session-side or driver-owned, and why each is safe to
     run after the terminal write;
   - the hold/transition contract in one paragraph (assignee held and status
     non-terminal for the whole run; terminal write + release are the last
     lifecycle action; a completed item with an empty assignee is audit-ready);
   - interruption semantics for abort, SIGTERM/SIGINT and SIGKILL (state left
     behind, whether the assignee is cleared or reclaimable, and how it is
     reclaimed);
   - post-push verification failure semantics (which verdict permits the
     terminal transition, and what happens to the item when the verdict is red
     or missing after a successful push).
4. If the chosen design differs from the parent's recorded assumption
   ("design A only re-orders, it does not add a suite run"), state the
   difference and its cost explicitly in the comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A design (A, B, C or a documented combination) is chosen and recorded in a comment on this item, with a rationale naming which of the parent AC1–AC5 each rejected option fails.
2. The ordered finalisation steps are written as an explicit numbered list covering everything `phase_finish` performs up to and including the terminal write and the read-back assertion, plus a separate list of steps that remain session-side or driver-owned with the reason each is safe after the terminal write.
3. The hold/transition contract is stated in one paragraph: assignee non-empty and status non-terminal for the whole run; terminal write and release are the run's last lifecycle action; a completed item with an empty assignee is audit-ready.
4. Interruption semantics are stated for abort, SIGTERM/SIGINT and SIGKILL: the state left behind, whether the assignee is cleared or reclaimable, and the command or path that reclaims it.
5. Post-push verification failure semantics are stated: the verdict required for the terminal transition, and the exact state left behind (status, assignee, comment, pushed commit) when the verdict is red or missing after a successful push.
6. No code or test file is modified by this item (verify with `git status` in the worktree).

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`

## Definition of Done

- Decision comment posted on this item and on the parent, naming the chosen
  design and the full contract.
- The contract is specific enough that the regression-test item
  ("Regression test: audit-dispatch hold ordering") and the implementation item
  ("Implement finalisation ordering in finish") need no further design input.
- UK English throughout.

# Goal

Add the failing-first regression test that proves parent AC2: during the
post-push phase of an implement run the work item is **not** a valid audit
candidate, and it becomes one only after the run's final lifecycle action.

Part of parent **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** (Only mark as complete when fully complete).
Test-first: this test is written and observed to **fail** against the current
`phase_finish` before the implementation item changes behaviour.

## Context

The race: `phase_finish` writes `completed`/`in_review` and releases the
assignee inside its `StatusLifecycle` block, then returns; `SKILL.md` Step 9
still requires the read-only post-push verification, worktree cleanup and the
completion comment afterwards. The herdr downtime dispatcher's
`selectAuditCandidate` (ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts`)
excludes only soft-deleted, freshly-audited, child, producer-review and
**assignee-held** items, so the item is dispatchable the moment `finish` exits.

## Scope

`skill/implement/tests/` only — one new test module. **No production behaviour
change** (that is the implementation item's job).

## Work

1. Follow the stub/runner harness style of
   `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`: patch the external
   boundaries (git, build runner, gate suite, worktree removal, the `wl`/
   `StatusLifecycle` store) and assert on observable outcomes — the recorded
   lifecycle calls, the store writes in order, and the returned report.
2. Model audit candidacy with a small, documented, test-local predicate that
   mirrors the dispatcher's documented filters (soft-delete, audit freshness,
   `parentId`, `needsProducerReview`, assignee hold, recency window), with a
   comment naming the ContextHub source. **Do not re-implement `implement.py`
   logic** — drive the real `phase_finish`.
3. Assert the ordering: record every store write and every post-push step
   (post-push verification, completion comment, cleanup) in a single ordered
   timeline, then assert that the item is not an audit candidate at each
   intermediate checkpoint and becomes one exactly once, after the final
   lifecycle action.
4. Assert the terminal write is the last lifecycle write and that the
   terminal-status read-back assertion ran after it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new test module under `skill/implement/tests/` exercises the real `phase_finish` state machine with only external boundaries patched, and contains no re-implementation of implement-phase logic.
2. The test builds one ordered timeline of store writes and post-push steps and asserts the item is not an audit candidate at every checkpoint before the final lifecycle action; a failure message names the offending checkpoint.
3. The test asserts the item becomes an audit candidate exactly once — after the final lifecycle action — and remains one afterwards.
4. The test asserts the final store state is `completed`/`in_review` with an empty assignee, and that `_assert_terminal_status` read-back ran after the terminal write.
5. The test fails against the current implementation for the documented reason (premature terminal transition / early assignee release); the observed failure output is recorded in a comment on this item.
6. The test passes once the implementation item lands, with no weakening of the assertions (verified by re-running it in that item).
7. The test file follows the shared test-writing guidelines (`skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`) — no self-referential simulation, no duplicate of existing core coverage.

8. **Parent AC trace (parent AC2).** **Observable audit-dispatch hold.** A regression test proves that during the post-push phase the item is not a valid audit candidate (non-empty assignee and/or non-`in_review` state), and that it becomes a valid candidate only after the final lifecycle step. The test exercises the real `implement.py` state machine (not a re-implementation) and asserts the transition ordering.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` (harness reference)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_finalisation_ordering.py` (new module)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (read only — `phase_finish`, `_assert_terminal_status`)
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`

## Definition of Done

- New test module committed in the worktree with the observed pre-fix failure
  recorded on this item.
- UK English throughout.

# Goal

Make `phase_finish` return only when the implement run is **fully complete**:
the post-push verification, the completion comment and the worktree cleanup
all happen *before* the terminal `completed`/`in_review` write and the assignee
release, which become the run's last lifecycle action.

Part of parent **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** (Only mark as complete when fully complete).
Implements the design recorded by the decision item; satisfied by the
regression-test item's test, unweakened.

## Context

Parent AC1: no `completed`/`in_review` + cleared-assignee state may be
observable while any implement-run step remains. Parent AC2 requires the
observable hold proven by the regression test. Parent constraints: preserve the
assignee-hold convention and release-by-default (SA-0MVVEDK2Q008NDUH /
SA-0MVVF6OJY000JZBL), preserve the terminal-status read-back guarantee
(`_assert_terminal_status`, OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58), preserve idempotence and
recovery, and do not change the herdr dispatcher.

## Scope

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (plus the minimum test updates the
ordering change genuinely requires). Docs are a separate item.

## Work

1. Implement the design recorded by the decision item (recommended default:
   verify-then-transition, unless the recorded decision says otherwise).
2. Move the read-only post-push full-suite verification (today `SKILL.md`
   Step 9's `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` cache-only check — it
   must **not** start a suite run) into `phase_finish` ahead of the
   `StatusLifecycle` exit, and record the verdict in the finish report
   (e.g. `report["steps"]["post_push_verification"]`).
3. Move the commit-hash completion comment into `phase_finish` ahead of the
   terminal write, preserving the audit-freshness ordering rule (comment before
   any audit persistence; SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM).
4. Keep process cleanup and worktree removal ahead of the terminal write on the
   non-deferred path. The deferred path (driven child session, `--keep-worktree`)
   stays deferred: document in a code comment that ownership of that cleanup
   passed to the driver/caller and it is therefore not a remaining run step.
5. Keep the terminal write and the `_assert_terminal_status` read-back as the
   last two lifecycle actions, in that order; the read-back must still fail
   loudly when the write does not stick, on both the push-with-diff and the
   no-op-push paths.
6. Handle a red or missing post-push verification verdict after a successful
   push: record the verdict in the report and in a work-item comment, refuse
   the terminal transition (item released to `open` with the assignee cleared
   and the pushed commit named), route the failure through the triage helper,
   and never revert or force-remove the pushed commit. A re-run of `finish`
   must converge (see the interruption item).
7. Preserve unchanged: push and post-push ancestry assertions, the
   per-repository finish lock, the main-checkout guard, the no-diff/no-op-push
   path, and every abort/safety-reset path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `phase_finish` performs, in order: post-push verification, completion comment, cleanup/worktree removal, terminal write, terminal-status read-back; each step is recorded in the finish report.
2. No `completed`/`in_review` + empty-assignee state is observable at any point while a required run step remains — proven by the regression-test item's test, unweakened (paste the passing run's summary in a comment).
3. The completion comment carries the pushed commit hash and is posted before the terminal write.
4. A red or missing post-push verification verdict after a successful push refuses the terminal transition: the item ends `open` with an empty assignee, a comment names the retained state and the pushed commit, a triage work item is created for the failure, and the pushed commit is neither reverted nor force-removed.
5. `_assert_terminal_status` still runs after the terminal write on both the push-with-diff and the no-op-push paths and still fails loudly when the store does not hold the terminal transition.
6. The assignee is released only with the terminal write (never earlier), and a producer hold the run does not own is never wiped (SA-0MVVF6OJY000JZBL).
7. Existing finish tests (`test_finish_no_diff_status.py`, `test_finish_gate_abort.py`, `test_finish_deferred_worktree_removal.py`, `test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py`, `test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py`, `test_finish_gate_*`) pass; any test updated because the ordering intentionally changed is named and the change explained in a comment on this item.
8. Build → changed-scope test → commit order is followed, and the commit hash is recorded on this item and on the parent.

9. **Parent AC trace (parent AC1).** **No premature terminal transition.** The implement skill must not make an item observable as `completed`/`in_review` with a cleared assignee while any implement-run step remains to be performed. Concretely: while the session is still doing post-push verification, worktree cleanup, or the completion comment, the item is either still `in_progress` with the assignee held, or otherwise excluded from audit dispatch by an explicit, documented hold. The terminal transition and assignee release happen only as the implement run's last lifecycle action.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_finish`, `_assert_terminal_status`, push/ancestry assertions, `_should_defer_worktree_removal`)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_deferred_worktree_removal.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_finalisation_ordering.py` (from the regression-test item)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (read-only `--summary` cache check)
- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`

## Definition of Done

- Regression test green, existing finish tests green, build green.
- Post-push verification and completion comment now run inside `finish`; no
  required run step remains after `finish` returns except driver-/caller-owned
  worktree cleanup.
- UK English throughout.

data.description:
# Goal

Guarantee that an implement run interrupted before its final lifecycle action
leaves the item in a non-terminal, non-audit-ready state (`open`/`in_progress`)
with the held assignee cleared or reclaimable and a comment/read-back naming
the retained state — and that a re-run converges — satisfying parent AC3.

Part of parent **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** (Only mark as complete when fully complete).

## Context

Parent AC3: an interrupted run must never be stuck in `completed`/`in_review`
for work that did not finish, and the existing abort/safety-reset paths must
keep passing their tests. Parent constraints: never strand a worktree or a
held item; preserve idempotence/recovery; do not weaken the assignee-hold
convention.

## Scope

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` interruption/recovery paths and their
tests.

## Work

1. Audit every interruption path: `_handle_signal_cleanup` /
   `_safety_reset_if_in_progress`, `phase_abort`, the `RuntimeError` handler in
   `phase_finish`, and drive reconciliation (`_finalise_stranded_child`, the
   drive failure-recovery tiers).
2. Ensure each path leaves the item `open` (or `in_progress` and reclaimable)
   with the assignee cleared, and never `completed`/`in_review` when a required
   step did not run.
3. Record a comment (or an explicit report field plus a comment) that names the
   retained state: status, stage, whether the assignee was cleared, the pushed
   commit hash when the push already happened, and the command that resumes.
4. Prove re-running `finish` after an interruption converges: no duplicated
   completion comment, no duplicate terminal transition, no stranded worktree,
   no lingering hold — reusing the existing no-diff/no-op-push and push-recovery
   paths rather than adding a new state machine.
5. Add tests for the interruption and convergence paths, following the
   existing finish harness style.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An interruption after a successful push but before the final lifecycle write leaves status `open` (or `in_progress`), never `completed`/`in_review`, with an empty assignee.
2. The interruption records a comment (or report field plus comment) naming the retained state, the pushed commit hash and the resume command.
3. A SIGTERM/SIGINT interruption keeps the existing safety-reset behaviour: status reset to `open`, assignee cleared, worktree not stranded.
4. Re-running `finish` after an interruption converges to `completed`/`in_review` with the assignee released, without duplicating the completion comment or the terminal transition.
5. New tests cover the interrupted-after-push path, the SIGTERM cleanup path and the re-run convergence; all existing abort, safety-reset, deferred-worktree-removal and finish tests pass unchanged.
6. No interruption path leaves a work item claimed with a non-empty assignee in a non-terminal state without a recorded, documented reclamation path.

7. **Parent AC trace (parent AC3).** **Recoverable interruption.** An implement run interrupted before its final step leaves the item in a non-terminal, non-audit-ready state (`in_progress`/`open`) with the held assignee cleared or reclaimable, plus a comment/read-back that names the retained state — never stuck permanently in `completed`/`in_review` for work that did not finish. Existing abort/safety-reset paths keep passing their tests.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_handle_signal_cleanup`, `_signal_handler`, `_safety_reset_if_in_progress`, `phase_abort`, `phase_finish` exception handler, `_finalise_stranded_child`)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py` (new module)
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (read only — release semantics)

## Definition of Done

- New interruption/convergence tests green, existing abort/safety-reset tests
  green, build green.
- Commit hash recorded on this item and on the parent.
- UK English throughout.

# Goal

Prove parent AC5 — the full project test suite passes with the change — and
verify the parent's acceptance criteria are collectively covered before the
parent is advanced for review.

Part of parent **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** (Only mark as complete when fully complete).

## Context

Parent AC5 requires the full suite to pass, including the new regression tests
and all existing implement/status-lifecycle tests. Test execution must go
through the test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`) — never an ad-hoc
`pytest` invocation. The dev-push gate runs the full suite on pushes to `dev`
and caches the verdict; this item consumes and verifies that evidence.

## Scope

Verification only — no production code changes. Fixes discovered here belong to
the implementation items (or to triaged `test-failure` items).

## Work

1. After the implementation and documentation items have landed, run the test
   skill at full scope (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py --scope full`) and confirm
   the run is green on the pushed commit.
2. Triage every failure through the triage skill
   (`skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`) into a critical `test-failure`
   work item, link it from this item, and do not declare success until the tree
   is green.
3. Confirm the new audit-dispatch hold regression test and every existing
   `skill/implement/tests/` and `skill/shared/test_status_lifecycle.py` test
   pass.
4. Run the audit skill on the parent and record its verdict; name any unmet
   parent AC with the child item that covers it.
5. Record the evidence in a comment: commit hash, scope, pass/fail summary and
   the cache entry consumed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full-scope test run on the pushed commit is green, and the evidence (commit hash, scope, summary) is recorded in a comment on this item.
